item.title: Sharp Convergence Rate for stationary states of the Porous Medium Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we prove the sharp rate of convergence for stationary states of the porous medium equation with an external drift in the p-Wasserstein metric under very mild assumptions on the potential and for any $1\leq p\leq +\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Igor Pinheiro, Filippo Santambrogio

item.title: Wetting theorems in capillarity theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.19116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the uniform convergence of Plateau borders to Plateau singularities in the vanishing-volume limit of a soap film model based on capillarity theory. The results are formulated in the context a new type of local area minimizer that takes into account how a soap film locally separates its surrounding space.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Maggi, Michael Novack, Daniel Restrepo

item.title: Density of Products of Solutions and the Linearized Calder\'on Problem in an Analytic Background
item.description: arXiv:2610.19288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the linearization, with respect to zeroth-order perturbations, of the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of a formally self-adjoint elliptic operator $P=-\Delta_g+Q$ on a compact Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of dimension $n\geq 2$ with boundary, where $Q$ is of order at most one. Near a boundary point where the boundary, metric, and $P$ are analytic, we show that the linearized map is a classical analytic pseudodifferential operator of order $-1$ if and only if the zeroth-order perturbation $q$ extends analytically across the boundary. We also prove that local boundary data in an arbitrary open analytic boundary patch determines $q$ locally. In particular, if the measurement set meets every connected component of $M$, the local linearized DN map is injective on $L^\infty$ perturbations. Finally, we obtain a global completeness result for products of pairs of solutions whose boundary traces are supported in the measurement set. The global recovery proceeds by local steps using Runge approximation.
item.dc:creator: Leonard Busch, Tony Liimatainen, Gunther Uhlmann

item.title: Relative Entropy and the Inviscid Limit for Planar Shocks of the Multi-D Burgers' Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent work (arXiv:2610.10341), the authors introduced a framework for studying the vanishing viscosity limit for sequences of weak solutions of the multi-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes equations to planar shocks of the compressible Euler equations. In this paper, we introduce these methods and apply them to the multi-dimensional viscous Burgers' equation. We show that arbitrarily large viscous shocks enjoy $L^2$-stability among perturbations whose gradients in the directions transverse to the shock are controlled in an appropriate manner. As an application, we study the rate of convergence to the inviscid shock in the vanishing viscosity limit.
item.dc:creator: Geng Chen, Jeffrey Cheng, Alexis F. Vasseur, Yi Wang

item.title: Nondegeneracy and asymptotic behavior of type I blow-up for semilinear heat equations with general nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2610.19332v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the local asymptotic behavior of nonnegative type I blow-up solutions to semilinear heat equations with nonlinearities that need not be scale invariant. Using a quasi-similarity transformation adapted to the associated ordinary differential equation, we establish locally uniform convergence to a constant profile on the parabolic spatial scale near every interior blow-up point. Under a quantitative assumption on the nonlinearity at infinity, our results cover regularly varying nonlinearities in the Sobolev subcritical and critical ranges and, in one and two space dimensions, rapidly growing nonlinearities including double exponentials. A key ingredient in this analysis is a positive lower bound for the normalized solution at interior blow-up points. In fact, under weaker assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove this bound in arbitrary space dimension without assuming radial symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Yohei Fujishima, Ryoto Ichiya, Norisuke Ioku

item.title: Fractional elementary symmetric functions and Hessian estimates in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.19410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an endpoint Pucci maximum principle for domains in $\mathbb R^2$, formulated using a generalization of elementary symmetric polynomials to noninteger orders. As a result, we sharpen an earlier result of Astala, Iwaniec and Martin, and deduce a new Sobolev inequality for $q$-Hessians where $1 < q < 2$. The fractional elementary symmetric functions we use are derived through fractional differentiation. Their signed singular value extension coincides with the Burkholder functional introduced by Burkholder and gives us access to a local Burkholder inequality due to Astala, Iwaniec, Prause and Saksman, leading to a different proof of the Pucci maximum principle from the one in that used quasiconformal maps. We include an elementary real-variable proof of this local Burkholder inequality, obtained by combining a few known techniques from existing literature.
item.dc:creator: Gautam Neelakantan Memana, Neil S. Trudinger, Po-Lam Yung

item.title: Dirac Points in High-Contrast Dielectric Honeycomb Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.19426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Dirac points for a two-dimensional scalar Helmholtz equation in a periodic dielectric medium with two penetrable inclusions per honeycomb cell. In a joint small-inclusion and high-contrast regime, we reduce the Bloch eigenvalue problem to a two-dimensional interaction matrix and derive a two-term asymptotic expansion for the two relevant eigenvalues, uniformly for quasi-momenta separated from the reciprocal lattice. At a vertex K of the Brillouin zone, rotation and inversion-conjugation symmetries force these eigenvalues to coincide. A Schur-complement analysis of the exact operator pencil, together with a nonvanishing lattice Green-function coefficient, proves that the resulting double eigenvalue has a nonzero conical splitting and gives an asymptotic formula for the conical slope in the scaled eigenvalue. For fixed sufficiently large contrast, symmetry-preserving changes of variables and analytic perturbation theory then continue this Dirac point as the inclusion size varies: it remains nondegenerate except at a relatively closed discrete set of admissible sizes.
item.dc:creator: Yi Huang, Bowen Li, Ping Liu

item.title: Global solvability with arbitrary mass for a chemotaxis--fluid model with sensitivity growth between linear and quadratic
item.description: arXiv:2610.19453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T\times\mathbb R$ with density-dependent diffusion and chemotactic sensitivity growing like $n^{1+\alpha}$, where $0<\alpha<1$. The coefficients satisfy the constitutive relation of Painter and Hillen (Can. Appl. Math. Q. 2002; 10(4): 501--543). Near a sufficiently strong Couette flow, we prove global classical solvability and uniform density bounds for smooth initial data with arbitrary finite cell mass. A key ingredient is a joint energy estimate for the full density and the non-zero-mode vorticity, which preserves the positive nonlinear diffusion and avoids the mixed diffusion terms arising from separate estimates of the density modes. Bounded Fourier corrections yield enhanced dissipation within this energy, allowing the non-zero-mode density--fluid interactions to be controlled. For the density zero mode, which is not mixed by Couette transport, we observe that $\alpha<1$ allows one-dimensional interpolation to absorb its chemotactic production into diffusion for every finite mass. Together, these estimates control the nonlinear diffusion and fluid coupling without imposing a smallness condition on the initial cell mass.
item.dc:creator: Lili Wang

item.title: ${\mathcal R}$-boundedness of Riesz transforms and spectral multipliers of Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\LL = -\Delta + V$ be a Schr\"odinger operator with a non-negative potential. It is known that its associated Riesz transform $\nabla \LL^{-\sfrac{1}{2}}$ is bounded on $L^p(\RR^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$, with a bound independent of $V$. We prove more, namely that the set \[ \{ \nabla \LL^{-\sfrac{1}{2}},\ 0 \le V \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\RR^d) \} \] is ${\mathcal R}$-bounded on $L^p(\RR^d)$ for $p \in (1,2]$. We also prove the ${\mathcal R}$-boundedness on $L^p(\RR^d)$, for $p \in (1,\infty)$, of the spectral multipliers \[ { m(\LL),\ 0 \le V \in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\RR^d) } \] for any $m:[0, \infty) \to \CC$ satisfying a H\"ormander type condition. Our approach is based on the analysis of Schr\"odinger operators $-{\bf \Delta} + {\bf V}$ on vector-valued spaces $L^p(\RR^d,\ell^2)$. In particular, we prove heat kernel estimates, Riesz transform bounds, and spectral multiplier results.
item.dc:creator: El Maati Ouhabaz

item.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for Riesz transforms of elliptic operators and magnetic Schr\"odinger operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold and define a magnetic Schr\"odinger operator $\LL = ({\bf d}+ iA)^*({\bf d}+iA) + V$ where $A$ is a real $1$-differential form in $L^2_{loc}$ and $V \in L^1_{loc}$ is a nonnegative electric potential. We prove that the magnetic Riesz transform $({\bf d} + iA) \LL^{-\einhalb}$ is of weak type $(1,1)$ with bound at most $2$. It extends to a bounded operator on $L^p$ for $p \in (1, 2]$ with norm bounded by a constant $c_p$ depending only on $p$. It is then independent of the dimension of the manifold and independent of $A$ and $V$. We also prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for symmetric elliptic operators subject to various boundary conditions on rough domains of $\RR^d$. The proofs are based on a new weak type $(1,1)$ criterion for operators.
item.dc:creator: El Maati Ouhabaz

item.title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: A PDE-Constrained Variational Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.19580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a PDE-constrained variational problem for the optimal spatial distribution of a catalytic material reacting with a substrate in a biological or materials system. With a given catalyst concentration, the substrate concentration is determined by a reaction-diffusion equation. The reaction functional for the catalyst concentrations is defined to be the total reaction output, which is the product of catalyst and substrate concentrations. Both the linear and Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics are considered. We construct reaction-maximizing sequences through the localization of catalysts using barrier functions and show the non-existence of a global maximizer. We also derive the first and second variations of the reaction functional. By constructing a competing catalyst concentration, we show the non-existence of a local maximizer. Based on our analysis, we propose a regularized variational model and prove the existence of its global maximizer.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Yasir Feroz Khan, Bo Li

item.title: Sharp $L^q$ estimate of adjoint problem and Pucci conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.19633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L$ be a linear second-order elliptic operator satisfying a nondegeneracy condition. We establish sharp $L^q$ estimates for solutions of the adjoint problem associated with $L$ and, by duality, derive sharp $L^p$ estimates for solutions of $Lu = f$. In particular, this confirms a conjecture of Carlo Pucci.
item.dc:creator: Jui-Yun Hung, Nan Wu

item.title: Asymptotic stability and Rayleigh-Taylor instability of stratified states for the three-dimensional rotating primitive equations with gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.19740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the 3D rotating primitive equations with gravity in a horizontally periodic channel, with viscous horizontal velocity and no density diffusion. For every Coriolis parameter, stably stratified equilibria are asymptotically stable. Small compatible \(H^4\) perturbations yield global classical solutions with uniform \(H^4\) bounds. The oscillatory density and velocity decay like \((1+t)^{-1}\); the density converges at the same rate to a stratified profile, its horizontal mean faster. For small data, the limit profile is the decreasing vertical rearrangement of the initial density, the unique potential-energy minimizer among rearrangements, independent of rotation, viscosity, and initial velocity. Kinetic plus available potential energy is dissipated exactly by viscosity and decays like \((1+t)^{-2}\), and each fluid particle settles where the limit density equals its own. These rates are optimal for every rotation rate. The linearized problem has real, slowly decaying normal modes, viscously overdamped high-vertical-wavenumber internal gravity waves, whose small solutions show the \(H^r\) density rates \((1+t)^{-(1-r/4)}\), \(0\le r<4\), pressure rate \((1+t)^{-1}\), and energy rate \((1+t)^{-2}\) cannot be improved uniformly for small data. Key difficulties are the loss of a horizontal derivative in the vertical velocity, the failure of \(H^1(\mathbb T^2)\subset L^\infty\), and rotation-induced coupling of divergent and vortical motion, controlled at top order by a positive power of the initial low-order energy. If the stratification is unstable somewhere, every horizontal mode is linearly unstable with real growth rates and the equilibrium is nonlinearly unstable; rotation strictly lowers each growth rate, with an explicit Taylor-number bound depending on the horizontal wavelength, but leaves their supremum unchanged.
item.dc:creator: Yanlong Fan, Fengjie Luo, Yiqiu Mao, Quan Wang

item.title: Global well-posedness of the energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with additive L\'evy noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.19749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes global well-posedness for the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the three-dimensional torus with a class of additive L\'evy noises. For arbitrary deterministic initial data in the energy space, we construct probabilistically strong solutions that are pathwise unique in the critical solution class. Continuous dependence on initial data, convergence of finite-activity approximations, and a vanishing-noise limit hold on finite time intervals. When the effective noise is nonzero, quantitative bounds for mass exit times imply almost-sure unboundedness of the mass and exclude free scattering. The expected energy then admits a cubic lower bound in time. The analysis couples pathwise critical perturbation theory with energy estimates adapted to Poisson compensation and stopping-time arguments based on the exact mass balance.
item.dc:creator: Bin Liu, Fan Xu

item.title: On blow-up for the supercritical defocusing nonlinear scalar wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-time singularity formation for the scalar defocusing nonlinear wave equation $-\partial_t^2u+\Delta u=u^p$. First, for fixed $d\geq4$ and odd $p\geq3$, we establish a conditional blow-up result under the assumption that a smooth self-similar imploding profile exists for the leading-order relativistic Euler system, with associated normalized coefficients satisfying quantitative analytic radius conditions. Second, we verify both the profile and the analytic radius conditions in dimensions four and five for all sufficiently large odd $p$. Using finite speed of propagation, we obtain a dimension-independent threshold $p_0$ such that, for every $d\geq4$ and every odd $p\geq p_0$, finite-time blow-up occurs for some smooth, compactly supported, real-valued initial data. The proof combines a normalized formulation that separates the leading periodic oscillation from the unknown modulation, growth of the spatial analytic radius induced by an outgoing property, and frequency-dependent matrix multipliers that control the cumulative growth caused by the periodic linearized potential.
item.dc:creator: Feng Shao, Dongyi Wei, Zhifei Zhang

item.title: Free-Material Optimization in a Peridynamic World
item.description: arXiv:2610.19776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study free-material optimization for nonlinear bond-based nonlocal diffusion and its localization as the interaction horizon $\delta$ vanishes. Bond conductivities are subject to pointwise bounds and a global material budget constraint. After normalization, the asymptotic behavior of these problems is governed by the fraction $\theta_\delta$ of potentially active bonds that can be assigned the maximal conductivity. We identify three distinct limiting regimes. If $\theta_\delta\to0$, the normalized optimal values converge to those of the classical vanishing-material optimal design problem, equivalently formulated as a Lipschitz-constrained state problem or a measure-valued flux problem. For $\theta_\delta\to\theta\in(0,1)$, we obtain a directional local free-material problem governed by the upper tail of the directional $p$-strain over position-direction space. Thus the state variable localizes, while the limiting constitutive law retains an internal directional variable inherited from the bonds. If $\theta_\delta\to\theta\geq1$, the limit is the isotropic local $p$-Dirichlet problem. A convex minimax argument eliminates the normalized conductivity variable exactly, after which the analysis combines convex duality, nonlocal compactness, and $\Gamma$-convergence for convex integrands. We prove a unified $\Gamma$-convergence result for the reduced state energies whenever $\theta_\delta\to\theta\in[0,+\infty)$, yielding convergence of normalized optimal values and compactness and identification of optimal states throughout the full parameter range. At the vanishing-material endpoint, we additionally recover optimal measure-valued local fluxes from optimal nonlocal two-point fluxes.
item.dc:creator: Anton Evgrafov

item.title: Resolvent Expansions at All Spectral Thresholds for Three-Dimensional Discrete Schr\"odinger Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.19845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies resolvent expansions at all four spectral thresholds for the discrete Schr\"odinger operator $H=-\Delta+V $ on $\Z^3$, where $\Delta$ denotes the discrete Laplacian on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ and $V(n)$ is a real-valued decaying potential of $\mathbb{Z}^3$. At the thresholds 0, 4, 8, and 12, we first give a complete classification of the threshold types and derive the corresponding resolvent expansions in weighted $\ell^2$-spaces, including the non-generic cases of resonances and eigenvalues. As a result, we establish the Jensen-Kato type time-decay estimates of the evolution $e^{itH} P_{ac}(H)$ to discrete Schr\"odinger equations with thresholds singularities on $\Z^3$, with decay $O(t^{-3/2})$ when all thresholds are regular and $O(t^{-1/2})$ otherwise. These results provide a three-dimensional lattice analogue of the Jensen--Kato classical analysis at zero energy threshold on $\mathbb{R}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Yanhong Chen, Sisi Huang, Xiaohua Yao

item.title: A starlike 3-dimensional counterexample to the hot spots conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.19908v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a bounded Lipschitz domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is starlike about the origin and whose first positive Neumann eigenvalue is simple. A corresponding eigenfunction, after a choice of sign, has its unique global maximum at the origin. The construction uses domains with increasingly fine angular structure and convergence to a weighted eigenvalue problem whose first positive eigenfunction is radial.
item.dc:creator: Rami Atar, Krzysztof Burdzy

item.title: Persistence of the reaction term in an unbalanced fast reaction limit
item.description: arXiv:2610.19914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a fast reaction limit for a two-component reaction-diffusion system in which one component diffuses and the other does not. In the regime considered here, the nondiffusing component converges to zero as the reaction rate tends to infinity, while the reaction term has a nonzero limit. As a result, the limiting equation for the diffusing component retains a time-integral term. Our results cover both homogeneous Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. We prove convergence of the diffusing component and determine the limiting behavior of the reaction term and the rescaled nondiffusing component. The proof combines monotonicity with respect to the reaction rate with barrier estimates adapted to the time-integral term. Under an additional separation condition on the initial data, we also prove uniqueness of the limiting initial-boundary value problem.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Tsukamoto

item.title: Elliptic theory and dimension drop for operators with divergence-free form-bounded drifts in one-sided chord-arc domains
item.description:
arXiv:2610.19983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a boundary value and potential theory for elliptic operators \[ L=-\Div(A
abla)+\B\cdot
abla \] with form-bounded drift in one-sided chord-arc domains. Assuming that the positive part of $\Div\B$ has sufficiently small form bound, we establish local regularity estimates and solvability of the Dirichlet problem, and construct the associated harmonic measure. Under the additional assumption $\Div\B\le0$, we construct a Green's function and prove pointwise and gradient estimates. For the characteristic distributional identity with a Dirac mass at the pole to hold, we will additionally assume either $\Div\B=0$ or $\B\in L^{n,1}_{	extup{loc}}(\Omega)$. Moreover, in the divergence-free case, we obtain a local lower bound for the Green's function, CFMS estimates, doubling of harmonic measure, a comparison principle for nonnegative solutions with zero trace, and a change of pole formula. Finally, using AI, we construct, in the upper half-space, an operator of the form $-\Delta+\B\cdot
abla$ with $\B$ form-bounded and divergence-free, whose harmonic measure exhibits dimension drop.
item.dc:creator: Svitlana Mayboroda, Alberto Pacati

item.title: A Parametrization of Solutions to the Yamabe Equation with Isolated Singularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.19984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by a pioneering work by Caffarelli, Gidas, and Spruck, we study positive solutions to the Yamabe equation with nonremovable isolated singularities. It is known that there is a formal one-to-one correspondence between the collection of the solutions to the Yamabe equation with nonremovable isolated singularities and the collection of harmonic functions through formal infinite series determined by the harmonic functions. In this paper, we prove that these formal infinite series yield actual solutions to the Yamabe equation with a nonremovable isolated singularity. These solutions to the Yamabe equation have designated asymptotic behaviors determined by the harmonic functions. In a broader context, we provide a general method of constructing all solutions near their isolated singular points and all solutions near infinity.
item.dc:creator: Qing Han, Jui-Yun Hung, Nan Wu

item.title: Sharp Sobolev inequalities under first moment constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.20001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\geq2$ and $1<p<n$. We study sharp Sobolev inequalities on the round sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ for functions $u\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb{S}^n)$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb{S}^n}x|u|^{np/(n-p)}\,d\sigma=0$. We prove that \[ \|u\|_{L^{np/(n-p)}(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p \leq 2^{-p/n}S_{n,p}^p\|\nabla u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p+B\|u\|_{L^p(\mathbb{S}^n)}^p \] holds for all such functions with some $B=B(n,p)<\infty$ if and only if $1<p\leq2$ or $2<p<n<3p-2$, where $S_{n,p}$ is the optimal Euclidean Sobolev constant. This determines the exact range in which Aubin's inequality holds with the sharp gradient coefficient. For every $2\leq p<n$, we also establish the corresponding inequality with squared norms and gradient coefficient $2^{-2/n}S_{n,p}^2$. The gradient coefficient in each inequality is optimal. The proof combines stereographic averaging with quantitative stability of the Euclidean Sobolev inequality to obtain local second moment estimates that allow absorption of the localization errors.
item.dc:creator: Rupert L. Frank, Tianling Jin, Hua-Yang Wang, Jingang Xiong

item.title: Refined blow-up behavior for semilinear heat equations with arbitrarily fast growing nonlinearities
item.description: arXiv:2610.20013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study radially nonincreasing, positive blow-up solutions of a class of superlinear heat equations in the non-scale-invariant setting. This class contains nonlinearities with arbitrarily fast, super-exponential growth. Under suitable structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we derive the sharp global blow-up profile in the original space-time variables. More precisely, for positive nonlinearities $f$ satisfying $$ \lim_{X\to \infty}f'(X)G(X)= q\ge1\quad \quad \hbox{ where }\quad\quad G(X)=\int_{X}^{\infty}\frac{ ds}{f(s)}<\infty\quad\forall\ X>0, $$ and assuming either the time monotonicity $u_t\ge0$ holds or $q>\frac{p_S}{p_S-1}$, we have $$ u(x,t)=(1+o(1))\,G^{-1}\bigg(T-t+\frac{|x|^2}{4q|\log |x|^2|}\bigg), \quad \hbox{as $(x,t)\to (0,T)$.} $$ This estimate in particular provides the sharp final space profile and the corresponding refined space-time profile. Moreover, our result recovers the universal structure of the global blow-up profile, given by the resolvent $G^{-1}$ of the associated ODE evaluated at a time-space building block, which only depends on the limit $q$.
item.dc:creator: Loth Damagui Chabi

item.title: Stabilities of Background Perturbations for Compressible Adiabatic Flows through Porous Media in 3-D
item.description: arXiv:2610.20031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the background stability problem for three-dimensional compressible adiabatic flows through porous media. For two given equilibrium states $(\bar{P}^k,\vec{0},\bar{S}^k)$ ($k=0,1$), under the assumption of small initial perturbations around each equilibrium state, pointwise estimates of solutions for individual perturbation problems are obtained. Based on these pointwise structures, a comparison between two individual solutions could be applied and it is proved that the difference between two solutions depends continuously on the equilibrium distance $|\bar{P}^0-\bar{P}^1|+|\bar{S}^0-\bar{S}^1|$ as well as the initial perturbation difference, with additional decay rates, thereby establishing a nonlinear comparison principle for this system. Compared with previous works on background stability problems, it is the first time to obtain stabilities in the pointwise sense. Our main tools are Green's functions, a priori energy estimates, and refined decay estimates for higher-order derivatives.
item.dc:creator: Shijin Deng, Xiaochun Yang

item.title: Kernel representations of fractional gradient bilinear forms. Part I. Constant coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.20110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the representation of bilinear forms associated with Riesz fractional gradients by symmetric integral kernels. Motivated by [SS18, Open Problem 1.10], we give a complete description of the constant coefficient case. We prove that any symmetric representing kernel is uniquely determined and we derive its explicit formula in terms of the constant matrix $A$. This yields a sharp characterization of the matrices for which the kernel is either nonnegative or uniformly positive. In particular, [SS18, Open Problem 1.10] has a negative answer (even for constant matrices). We also identify a class of nonconstant antisymmetric divergence free perturbations that are invisible to the fractional bilinear form and hence leave the representing kernel unchanged. The general case of nonconstant matrices exhibits a substantially different behavior and will be the main subject of our forthcoming paper [DSV26].
item.dc:creator: Serena Dipierro, Caterina Sportelli, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: Topological degree for singular $N$-mean field equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Dirichlet $N$-mean field equation on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\geq2$, for every positive nonresonant parameter and singular exponents $-1<\alpha_i\leq0$. The formula depends only on the Euler characteristic of the domain and the weights $(1+\alpha_i)^{N-1}$. We also identify the homotopy type of every sufficiently negative variational sublevel with the corresponding weighted barycenter space. We prove quantization of interior concentration masses and exclude boundary concentration and residual diffuse mass. The degree computation uses common descent fields for nearby parameters, bounds for their trajectories, and a finite-dimensional comparison with the Euler characteristic of negative sublevels. Annular averaging and dilation provide local contractions, which are extended to establish the sublevel homotopy equivalence. The arguments apply to the nonlinear, possibly degenerate $N$-Laplacian with singular weights, without requiring a global Palais--Smale condition or isolation and nondegeneracy of solutions.
item.dc:creator: Mohameden Ahmedou, Zhongwei Tang, Heming Wang

item.title: Quantized slow blowup dynamics for the energy-critical Schr\"odinger map flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.20313v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the energy-critical Schr\"{o}dinger map into the 2-sphere: \[ \partial_{t}u = u\times\Delta u, \quad (t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{1+2}, \quad u(t,x)\in\mathbb{S}^2 \] for equivariant initial data of homotopy degree $k=1$. Given any integer $L\in\mathbb{N}_+$, we exhibit a set of initial data arbitrarily close to the ground state harmonic map in the energy norm such that the corresponding solution blows up in finite time with a quantized rate \[ \lambda(t)\sim \frac{\left(T-t\right)^L}{\left|\log(T-t)\right|^{\frac{2L}{2L-1}}} \quad\mbox{as}\ \ t\uparrow T. \] Our proof is inspired by the techniques developed for the energy-critical harmonic map heat flow in a similar context by Rapha{\"e}l and Schweyer~[Anal. PDE 7 (2014), 1713--1805]. However, its adaptation to a Schr\"{o}dinger-type equation requires the introduction of a new energy-Virial-Morawetz Lyapunov functional tailored to quantized slow blowup dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Jendrej, Jitao Xu, Xu Yuan, Lifeng Zhao

item.title: Transference principles for divergence sets of dispersive equations and their applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.20480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study the fractal refinement of the Carleson's problem: (1) We introduce an equivalence relation on linear dispersive PDEs on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ based on the high-frequency oscillation of their Fourier multipliers, proving that equations in the same class share the same Hausdorff dimension of divergence sets. As applications, we estimate these dimensions for abstract dispersive families. Consequently, we recover known $1$-dimensional results for linearized Boussinesq and Beam propagations, while establishing new results for both in higher dimensions and for Klein-Gordon propagations in all dimensions. (2) Next, we study the effect of radial symmetry by obtaining dimension estimates for fractional Schr\"odinger equations with concave phase and radial initial data. Applying a transference principle, dimension estimates are extended to families of abstract dispersive equations. As special cases, we recover the known result for the Beam propagation and also obtain new results for the linearized Boussinesq and the Klein-Gordon propagations in the radial setting. (3) We study analogues of (2) for the $3$-dimensional real hyperbolic space by obtaining dimension estimates for a wide class of dispersive propagations: the Schr\"odinger, fractional Schr\"odinger (with convex and concave phases), Beam, linearized Boussinesq, Wave and Klein-Gordon equations. This is the first result of its kind, outside the setting of flat Euclidean geometry. Our arguments are based on an inter-spatial transference principle of geometric-analytic flavour. In the process, we also obtain a quantitative result on the singular sets of Sobolev functions, in the spirit of \v{Z}ubrini\'c, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Utsav Dewan

item.title: Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator on Lipschitz graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant. The essential tool is the Coifman--McIntosh--Meyer theorem, applied to a holomorphic family of complex curves, together with the Cauchy integral formula on a contour surrounding the interval of secant slopes. We also include a simpler version of the argument that gives $O(\log n)$ and explains why the contour has the shape it has.
item.dc:creator: Joan Hern\'andez, Joan Mateu, Laura Prat

item.title: Fast separation of Euler and Navier--Stokes flows in two dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.20540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the long-time validity of the inviscid limit problem by measuring when the two-dimensional ideal fluid ceases to accurately approximate a slightly viscous fluid with the same initial datum. We construct a stationary solution of the Euler equation from which the Navier--Stokes solution separates at a time scale proportional to the logarithm of the inverse viscosity, achieving the fastest separation from Euler steady states.
item.dc:creator: Siming He, Yupei Huang, Jincheng Yang

item.title: All Serrin bands are unduloidal
item.description: arXiv:2610.20581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that any Serrin domain in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with two boundary components is a member of the canonical unduloidal family
item.dc:creator: Laurent Hauswirth, Pablo Mira

item.title: On optimal Wannier decay in dimension three
item.description: arXiv:2610.19195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay $\mathcal{O}(|x|^{-5/2})$. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.
item.dc:creator: Simon Becker, Zhongkai Tao, Mengxuan Yang

item.title: The fence conjecture for convex projective polygons
item.description: arXiv:2610.19664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the fence conjecture of Dumas and Wolf: for a convex projective polygon with at least five vertices, every zero of the Pick differential lies in the interior of the region obtained by cutting off the triangles at consecutive triples of vertices. The proof gives a stronger estimate for arbitrary properly convex domains. In affine-sphere coordinates normalized at a Pick zero, the domain contains the closed disk of radius $2^{-1/4}$ and its closure lies in the open disk of radius $2^{1/4}$, unless it is a rotated square. The proof compares the canonical Monge-Amp\`ere potential of the domain with that of a normalized square. Their third-order contact gives alternating local sign sectors. A planar separation argument and the maximum principle show that the negative sectors belong to four distinct components, each meeting a different side of the square. Rotation gives the inner disk bound, and conormal duality gives the outer bound. Both constants are optimal for the class of properly convex domains normalized at a Pick zero. The argument requires neither boundary smoothness nor any restriction on the multiplicity of the Pick zero.
item.dc:creator: Erxiao Wang

item.title: Coupled reciprocal-sum inequalities for Neumann eigenvalues in rank-one symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a rank-one symmetric space of compact or noncompact type and real dimension $m=kn$, where $k\in\{1,2,4,8\}$ is the real dimension of the underlying division algebra. Meng and Wang proved sharp isoperimetric inequalities for reciprocal sums of the first $p$ or $\ell$ nonzero Neumann eigenvalues, with indices strictly below $m$ in the nonconstant-curvature cases. We keep the whole $m$-dimensional transplanted first eigenspace of an equimeasurable geodesic ball and treat its mass and stiffness forms as a coupled generalized eigenvalue problem. For every bounded connected smooth domain in a noncompact rank-one symmetricspace we prove the full sharp estimate \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}\frac{1}{\mu_j(\Omega)} \ge \frac{m}{\mu_1(B)}, \] where $B$ is a geodesic ball with $|B|=|\Omega|$; equality characterizes geodesic balls. The Hopf-direction contribution is encoded by a positive, unital, trace-preserving projection on symmetric matrices, and the finite-dimensional closure is supplied by a positive-projection Jensen inequality. In compact type, under the localization hypothesis of Meng--Wang, the same full estimate is obtained whenever $\cot^2 R\ge k-1$, where $R$ is the radius of the comparison ball, as well as in the isotropic endpoint cases and for Hopf-balanced angular second moment. Consequently the complete $m$-term inequality holds for all complex and quaternionic projective spaces under the original localization assumption, and for the Cayley plane when $R\le \arctan(1/\sqrt7)$. In the remaining admissible Cayley interval we exhibit a finite-dimensional obstruction showing that the affine tangent-matrix bounds alone cannot yield the full trace estimate. This obstruction concerns the proof mechanism and is not a counterexample to the unresolved spectral inequality.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Meng

item.title: Interior smoothness and zero-variance geometry for finite-maturity Heston American puts
item.description: arXiv:2610.20000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite-maturity American puts in the Heston model without the Feller condition. At positive variance, the exercise boundary is smooth and strictly decreasing in remaining maturity and variance. At zero variance, the endpoint is locally Lipschitz in remaining maturity, the boundary moves with bounded speed in maturity uniformly down to zero variance, and it extends continuously to the axis. Each boundary slice at positive maturity has a regular $C^1$ closure tangent to the zero-variance axis, its stock threshold has variance derivative tending to minus infinity, and both partial derivatives of the inverse boundary graph vanish along the slice. The continuation premium at the axis contact stock is of order variance, and as a consequence smooth fit fails in the variance direction at the axis. At expiry the whole boundary, including its axis edge, converges to the strike. We give quantitative boundary gap bounds, an exact limiting weighted boundary Hessian, and vertical identities retaining the maturity term. Exact boundary gap equivalents remain open.
item.dc:creator: Junkee Jeon, Takwon Kim, Jehan Oh

item.title: A semi-discrete scheme for horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.20054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The horizontal mean curvature flow is a geometric evolution associated with the horizontal perimeter in sub-Riemannian spaces. In this paper, we introduce a minimizing movement scheme for this flow in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}$, and prove the existence of a flat flow which is locally $1/2$-H\"older continuous in time, with respect to the $L^1$-distance. The construction applies to arbitrary bounded sets of finite horizontal perimeter and does not require smoothness or symmetry of the initial datum.
item.dc:creator: A. Cesaroni, M. Novaga, P. Pozzi

item.title: KPP type reaction--diffusion equations in narrow tubes with degenerating boundary and generalized second order operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.20081v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a reaction--diffusion equation with Kolmogorov--Petrovskii--Piskunov (KPP) nonlinearity and Neumann boundary conditions in a narrow tube $G^{\varepsilon,\delta}\subset\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}$ of width of order $\varepsilon$. The tube is chosen from a family indexed by a second parameter $\delta>0$, whose boundary $\partial G^{\delta}$ is smooth for each $\delta>0$ but degenerates as $\delta\downarrow0$. In the iterated limit $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ followed by $\delta\downarrow0$ the problem becomes a Cauchy problem on the line whose spatial operator is a generalized second order differential operator $D_{v}D_{u}$ in the sense of Feller, rather than a classical second order elliptic operator. Solutions of the limiting problem need not be differentiable in $x$, so they must be understood in a generalized sense. Using the Feynman--Kac representation, we prove that the limiting problem has a unique generalized solution. When the cross sectional volume is bounded above and below, we also prove that this solution is H\"older continuous in $t$ with exponent $1/2$, locally uniformly in $x$, whenever it is Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Under the same volume bounds, this Lipschitz condition holds when the initial function and the nonlinearity are Lipschitz continuous in $x$. Finally we prove that the solutions in the narrow tubes converge to the generalized solution uniformly on compact time intervals in the same iterated limit if the tube, the initial function, and the nonlinearity are periodic in $x$.
item.dc:creator: Hyejin Kim

item.title: A note on the failure of Payne's inequality on manifolds with boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.20097v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that Payne's conjecture on the comparison between Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues and buckling eigenvalues does not hold on flat and hyperbolic cylindrical surfaces and on (round) hemispheres.
item.dc:creator: Davide Buoso, Vladimir Lotoreichik

item.title: Emulating the Darcy Solution Operator by Heat-Semigroup Functional Calculus and Pointwise Products
item.description:
arXiv:2610.20106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We approximate the solution operator $(a,f)\mapsto u$ of $-\operatorname{div}(a
abla u)=f$ by operator networks whose only primitives are heat-semigroup functions of a fixed reference operator and pointwise products. The main result is an emulation theorem on strongly local Dirichlet spaces with a spectral gap and a Bakry--'Emery bound $\mathrm{BE}(-K,\infty)$: an explicit scheme reaches $\dot H^1$-error $\varepsilon$ uniformly over coefficients with bounded carr'e du champ and bounded generator image and over $L^2$ data, with parameters depending only on the coefficient bounds, the accuracy and $K$; on the torus this gives a $C^2$-type coefficient class with constants independent of the dimension. The torus version refines this to Wiener classes of fractional regularity $A^{1+	heta}$, with an explicit rate attained by the scheme's product-defect block. The scheme unrolls the Laplacian-preconditioned Richardson iteration, controls each inexact step in the operator norm of $\dot H^1$ without Galerkin truncation, and synthesises the coupling $
abla a\cdot
abla u$ from the product defect of one heat layer. All parameters are explicit; the results are approximation theorems for continuum operators.
item.dc:creator: Dawid Hanrahan

item.title: Model order reduction of HDG discretizations for harmonic wave propagation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20145v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose and analyze a projection-based model reduction method for the rapid and reliable solution of time-harmonic acoustic wave propagation problems over a frequency band, with particular emphasis on seismic applications. The high-fidelity model is based on a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) discretization, formulated as a generalized saddle-point system coupling the volume and trace unknowns. The basis construction combines residual-based greedy sampling of the frequency parameter, enrichment with frequency derivatives of the HDG solution, and proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) compression. We establish the well posedness of both the high-fidelity and reduced problems and characterize their stability with inf-sup constants. We investigate the interaction between static condensation, inherent to the HDG discretization, and projection onto the reduced spaces, characterizing its implications for the reduced formulation and approximation errors. Since these operations do not commute in general, we derive a priori error estimates for both the trace and volume variables to quantify the gap between the two operations. We further identify a lifting condition on the volume reduced space that eliminates these gaps and yields a trace error estimate independent of the volume approximation error. Numerical experiments on the two-dimensional Marmousi model and a three-dimensional heterogeneous medium, with more than $10^{7}$ unknowns, illustrate the theoretical estimates and show that the reduced model achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude compared to the high-fidelity solver.
item.dc:creator: H\'el\`ene Barucq, Florian Faucher, Ha Pham, Ishak Tifouti

item.title: Geometric $C^1$-stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.20265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove stability of geodesic spheres under volume-preserving mean curvature flow in the simply connected space forms under genuinely first-order geometric assumptions. The initial hypersurface is required to lie in a sufficiently thin annulus around a geodesic sphere and to have outward normal making a small angle with the radial direction. No convexity, mean convexity, initial curvature bound, or H\"older control of the normal is assumed. The main ingredient is a quantitative Alexandrov reflection argument that converts these initial assumptions into a strong reflection property preserved by the flow. The resulting radial and angular control allows us to derive estimates for the mean curvature and the full second fundamental form, and hence long-time existence, eventual convexity, and smooth exponential convergence to a geodesic sphere. In hyperbolic space, the eventual convexity can be strengthened to horospherical convexity. The reflection threshold also yields a quantitative estimate for the displacement of the limiting centre. For Lipschitz initial hypersurfaces, we develop a separate positive-time curvature estimate that is uniform along smooth approximations. This produces an instantaneously smooth evolution with the same eventual convexity and smooth exponential convergence.
item.dc:creator: Esther Cabezas-Rivas, Carlo Sinestrari

item.title: Allen--Cahn and mean curvature flows from Clifford hypersurfaces to equators
item.description: arXiv:2610.20453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this short note, using OpenAI's resolution of the Solomon--Yau conjecture, we extend our joint work with Pedro Gaspar to all dimensions $n\geq2$. We construct eternal Allen--Cahn flows on $S^{n+1}$ connecting approximations of any prescribed least-area Clifford hypersurface and equatorial sphere. We also construct infinitely many eternal integral Brakke flows from least-area Clifford hypersurfaces to equatorial spheres.
item.dc:creator: Jingwen Chen

item.title: A Scale-Critical $\mu<\frac38$ Extension Principle for Spherically Symmetric Einstein-Scalar Field System
item.description: arXiv:2610.20468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new quantitative, scale-critical $C^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. We derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{O}$ of the center. Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $\mu=2m/r$ satisfies $\sup\mu<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $\mu$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $\mu\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $\mu<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.
item.dc:creator: Xinliang An, Haoyang Chen, Jaydeep Singh

item.title: An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
item.description: arXiv:2610.20469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $\alpha'$ with $\alpha'=\partial_v\alpha/\partial_vr$ and $\alpha=\partial_v(r\phi)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein. As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.
item.dc:creator: Xinliang An, Haoyang Chen, Taoran He

item.title: Quantization analysis of Moser-Trudinger equations in the Poincar\'e disk and applications
item.dc:creator: Lu Chen, Qiaoqiao Hua, Guozhen Lu, Shuangjie Peng, Chunhua Wang

item.title: Well- and ill-posedness of the Cauchy problem for semi-linear Schr\"odinger equations on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2501.04205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for semi-linear Schr\"odinger equations on the torus $\mathbb T$. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition on the polynomial nonlinearity for the Cauchy problem to be well-posed in the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb T)$ for $s>\frac 52$. For the well-posedness, we use the energy estimates and the gauge transformation. For the ill-posedness, we prove the non-existence of solutions to the Cauchy problem.
item.dc:creator: Toshiki Kondo, Mamoru Okamoto

item.title: Lipschitz regularity of fractional $p$-Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2504.09457v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we investigate the H\"{o}lder regularity of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation of the form $(-\Delta_p)^s u=f$ where $p>1, s\in (0, 1)$ and $f\in L^\infty_{\rm loc}(\Omega)$. Specifically, we prove that $u\in C^{0, \gamma_\circ}_{\rm loc}(\Omega)$ for $\gamma_\circ=\min\{1, \frac{sp}{p-1}\}$, provided that $\frac{sp}{p-1}\neq 1$. In particular, it shows that $u$ is locally Lipschitz for $\frac{sp}{p-1}>1$. Moreover, we show that for $\frac{sp}{p-1}=1$, the solution is locally Lipschitz, provided that $f$ is locally H\"{o}lder continuous. Additionally, we discuss further regularity results for the fractional double-phase problems.
item.dc:creator: Anup Biswas, Erwin Topp

item.title: The Modified Camassa--Holm Equation with Step-Like Boundary Conditions: A Characterization of Existence
item.description: arXiv:2507.02100v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the modified Camassa-Holm equation \[ u_t+\left((u^2-u_x^2)m\right)_x=0,\quad m:= u-u_{xx}, \quad t>0,\ \ -\infty<x<+\infty \] subject to the step-like initial data: $u(x,0)\to A_1$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u(x,0)\to A_2$ as $x\to+\infty$, where $0<A_1<A_2$. First, using the Riemann--Hilbert approach, we establish the global solvability of the corresponding problem in the reciprocal $(y,t)$-variables. Then the reconstruction in the original $(x,t)$-variables is obtained under a positivity condition expressed in terms of the solution of the associated Riemann--Hilbert problem.
item.dc:creator: I. Karpenko, D. Shepelsky, G. Teschl

item.title: Higher integrability for parabolic PDEs with generalized Orlicz growth
item.description:
arXiv:2511.19758v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove higher integrability of the gradient of weak solutions to nonlinear parabolic systems whose prototype is \[ \partial_t u-\mathrm{div}\Big( rac{\varphi'(z, |
abla u|)}{|
abla u|}
abla u\Big) =0, \qquad u=(u^1,\dots,u^N), \] where $\varphi$ is a generalized Young function. Special cases of our main theorem include previously known results for the $p$-growth, the variable exponent and the double phase growth. Also included are previously unknown borderline double phase growth and perturbed variable exponent growth, among others. The problem is controlled by a natural requirement of comparison of $\varphi$ between points in intrinsic parabolic cylinders via an (A1)-condition, which unifies disparate conditions from the special cases. Moreover, we handle both the singular and degenerate cases at the same time, providing a unified proof of of a reverse H"older type inequality.
item.dc:creator: Peter H\"ast\"o, Jihoon Ok

item.title: Fractional hypocoercivity in bounded domains in the anomalous diffusion limit
item.description: arXiv:2512.20222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide quantitative stability results for several dissipative linear kinetic equations with heavy-tailed equilibria in different geometries. Moreover, the approach, inspired by the so-called $L^2$-hypocoercivity method, is robust enough to provide estimates that are uniform in the anomalous diffusion limit. It applies to bounded domains with either periodic or general Maxwell boundary conditions (ranging from the pure specular to the pure diffusive case) as well as to the whole-space case. In addition, our framework accommodates linear collisional operators whose coefficients depend on the position.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Herda, Marc Pegon, Isabelle Tristani

item.title: On the interplay between $(p,q)$-growth and $x$-dependence of the energy integrand: a limit case
item.description: arXiv:2602.12033v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral funtionals of the form \[ \int_\Omega F(x, Dz)\,dx, \] where $\Omega$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$. The energy density $F(x,\xi)$ satisfies $(p,q)-$growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable and belongs to the Sobolev class $W^{1,\phi}$, with $\phi(t)=t^r\log^\alpha(e+t),$ $r\ge n$, $\alpha\ge 0$, as a function of the $x$ variable, under the condition $$ 1\le\frac{q}{p} \le 1 + \frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{r}. $$ We present a unified approach that covers the limit case $$ \frac{q}{p} = 1 + \frac{1}{n} - \frac{1}{r} $$ and retrieves the results in \cite{EMM16} and in \cite{CGHPdN20}.
item.dc:creator: M. Eleuteri, P. Marcellini, E. Mascolo, A. Passarelli di Napoli

item.title: Well-posedness of the heat equation in domains with topological transitions
item.description: arXiv:2603.05403v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze a linear parabolic equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions posed in domains whose evolution may involve topological transitions. The domains are described as sublevel sets of a smooth space-time level set function, allowing for transitions such as domain splitting and merging and the creation or vanishing of islands and holes. We introduce anisotropic space-time function spaces that extend the classical Bochner spaces used in cylindrical domains and establish key functional-analytic properties of these spaces, including the density of compactly supported smooth functions. This framework enables the application of the Babu\v{s}ka-Banach theorem, yielding existence, uniqueness, and a priori estimates for weak solutions. The analysis applies to domain evolutions generated by level set functions with isolated nondegenerate critical points, which correspond to the generic topology changes classified by Morse theory in two and three spatial dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Maxim Olshanskii, Arnold Reusken

item.title: Finite-time blow-up for the Geng--Xue system with an application to the three-component Degasperis--Procesi system
item.description: arXiv:2603.22952v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove finite-time blow-up for the Geng--Xue system with initial data satisfying $u_0\in W^{p,q}(\R)$ and $n_0\in L^{r'}(\R)$ at Sobolev regularity $s\geq2$, where $n=v-v_{xx}$. A cancellation in the balance law for $nu_x$ yields closed convolution estimates that do not depend on an a priori uniform bound for $u_x$. These estimates control $v$ along a characteristic and give an explicit condition on the initial slope, together with an upper bound on the lifespan. The proof does not use conservation laws. For the three-component Degasperis--Procesi system, the same argument applies to $nu_x+\rho^2-\bar\rho^2$, where $\bar\rho\in[0,1]$ is a constant density background. We also prove local well-posedness for this system in $H^{s-1}(\R)\times H^s(\R)\times H^s(\R)$ for $s>\frac32$, and a blow-up criterion in $B^1_{2,1}(\R)\times B^2_{2,1}(\R)\times B^2_{2,1}(\R)$.
item.dc:creator: Song Liu, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy
item.description: arXiv:2604.04776v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we establish optimal $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity up to the boundary for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations with double phase degeneracy law and oblique boundary conditions. The approach developed here relies on first deriving uniform boundary H\"older estimates for perturbed models with oblique boundary data in ``almost $C^{1}$-flat'' domains. Building upon these estimates, the desired regularity is obtained through a compactness and stability framework for viscosity solutions. As a byproduct of our analysis, we determine the optimal H\"older exponent for solutions when the governing operator is quasiconvex or quasiconcave. In addition, we establish an improved regularity result along vanishing points of the source term.
item.dc:creator: Junior da Silva Bessa, Jehan Oh

item.title: Lipschitz regularity for fractional $p$-Laplacian with coercive gradients
item.description: arXiv:2604.07489v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article we study nonlinear nonlocal equations with coercive gradient nonlinearity of the form \[ (-\Delta_{p})^{s}u(x)+H(x,\nabla u)=f , \] where $f$ is Lipschitz continuous and the Hamiltonian $H$ satisfies the coercivity condition \[ H(x,\xi)\;\geq\;\theta|\xi|^{m}-\theta_{1} \qquad\text{for all } x,\xi\in\mathbb{R}^n, \] for some constants $\theta,\theta_{1}>0$ and $m>1$. Under an additional local Lipschitz assumption on $H$, we show that every viscosity solution $u$ is locally Lipschitz continuous provided that \[ \text{either}\; sp>p-2\; \text{or}\; 1<p<m+1. \] We also establish H\"older and Lipschitz continuity of subsolutions, for which boundedness of $f$ alone suffices. Furthermore, when $f=0$ and $H$ is independent of $x$, we prove that the equation admits only the trivial solution within the class of bounded solutions, for all $m,p\in(1,\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Anup Biswas, Aniket Sen, Erwin Topp

item.title: The Three-Dimensional Divergence-Curl Problem with Homogeneous Boundary Conditions and Pseudo-Harmonic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2605.10422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article addresses the solvability of the three-dimensional divergence-curl problem with a no-slip boundary condition. A solvability criterion is derived as an orthogonality condition of the vorticity function to pseudo-harmonic fields. A countable family of such fields, sufficient for the solvability of the three-dimensional problem in the exterior of a sphere, is also presented.
item.dc:creator: A. V. Gorshkov

item.title: Multi parameter identification in the nonlinear periodic Westervelt equation
item.description: arXiv:2605.15946v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nonlinear ultrasound imaging leverages harmonic wave generation to enhance contrast and spatial resolution beyond the capabilities of conventional linear techniques. This behavior is commonly modeled by the Westervelt equation, which captures finite-amplitude acoustic wave propagation in heterogeneous media. In this work, we investigate an inverse problem for a periodic nonlinear Westervelt equation in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $d\in\{2,3\}$ with spatially varying coefficients and Robin-type boundary conditions. The objective is to simultaneously reconstruct the sound speed, diffusivity, and nonlinearity parameters from (partial) boundary measurements. We first establish the Fr\'echet differentiability of the forward solution operator with respect to the unknown parameters, providing a rigorous analytical foundation for parameter identification. To address uniqueness, we introduce a reference-state framework and prove linearized uniqueness of an all-at-once forward operator without requiring the reference states to satisfy the governing equation. Building on these results, we develop an iterative reconstruction scheme based on a frozen Newton-type method, supported by an exact range invariance property. Numerical simulations are presented to illustrate the feasibility and performance of the proposed approach.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Rainer, Barbara Kaltenbacher

item.title: Decay estimates for the two-dimensional Beam equation with potentials
item.description: arXiv:2606.16793v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper establishes time decay estimates for the following two-dimensional beam (plate) equation with a decaying real-valued potential $V$: \begin{equation*} \partial_t^2 u + (\Delta^2 + V) u = 0, \qquad u(0,x)=f(x),\quad \partial_t u(0,x)=g(x). \end{equation*} When zero is a regular point or a first-kind resonance of $H=\Delta^2+V$, we first prove sharp $L^1\to L^\infty$ estimates for the solution operators: \begin{align*} \left\|\cos(t\sqrt{H})P_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)\right\|_{L^1\to L^\infty} + \left\|\frac{\sin(t\sqrt{H})}{t\sqrt{H}}P_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)\right\|_{L^1\to L^\infty} \lesssim \frac{1}{|t|}, \end{align*} and obtain an enhanced decay $(|t|\log|t|)^{-1}$ in logarithmically weighted spaces $L^1_\omega\to L^\infty_{-\omega}$ with $\omega(x)=\log(2+|x|)$. For second-kind resonances of $H$ (the bi-Laplacian $\Delta^2$ belongs to this class), a non-zero trace moment $\langle |x|^2V,\phi\rangle\neq0$ for some second-kind resonance function $\phi$ induces severe threshold singularities, worsening the $L^1\to L^\infty$ estimate to $|t|^{-1}(\log|t|)^2$. Finally, for third-kind resonances or a zero eigenvalue, we prove that the presence of $d$-wave resonance leads to the worst $L^1\to L^\infty$ decay rate $\sim(\log|t|)^{-1}$. Several improved estimates are also obtained without a $d$-wave resonance. In particular, in the pure eigenvalue case (i.e., neither $d$-wave nor $p$-wave resonance), both propagators recover the optimal unweighted $L^1\to L^\infty$ estimate $|t|^{-1}.$
item.dc:creator: Shuangshuang Chen, Han Cheng, Zijun Wan, Xiaohua Yao

item.title: Monotonicity Property of Non-Archimedean Heat Equation
item.description: arXiv:2606.20567v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the monotone dependence of the heat kernel corresponding to the Vladimirov-Taibleson non-Archimedean fractional differentiation operator $D^\alpha$ on the order $\alpha$.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra V. Antoniouk, Anatoly N. Kochubei

item.title: Microlocal defect functionals in VMO: Geometric localisation and applications to highly heterogeneous media
item.description: arXiv:2607.04294v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the concept of microlocal defect functionals to test functions belonging to the space $\mathrm{L}^\infty\cap\mathrm{VMO}_c$. Following L.~Tartar's remark that an extension of such concepts to $\mathrm{VMO}$ spaces should be possible, we establish a functional-analytic framework for this extension within the $\mathrm{L}^p-\mathrm{L}^q$ setting. Because the topological dual of $\mathrm{VMO}$ is the Hardy space $\mathcal{H}^1$, the resulting object takes the form of an H-distribution rather than a non-negative Radon measure. By assuming strict H\"older conjugate inequalities, we use the John-Nirenberg inequality over localized domains to construct these functionals. We show that the functional acts as a distribution on the inductive limit topology of the test spaces, giving geometric localisation principles for equations with rough $\mathrm{VMO}$ coefficients, that is, coefficients admitting sharp transitions of vanishing mean oscillation. We illustrate the framework in three settings: stratified transport, zero-order non-local cross-phase energies, and sub-critical acoustic scattering in high-contrast media. These differ in the nonlinearity generating the companion sequence but share a common geometric conclusion, since in each case the macroscopic energy defect is confined to the characteristic variety of the underlying flow, being supported where $\sum_j a_j({\bf x})\xi_j=0$.
item.dc:creator: Marin Mi\v{s}ur

item.title: Homothetic Self-Similar Solutions to the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
item.description: arXiv:2607.12159v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate homothetic forward self-similar solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations: the solutions $\overline{U}$ for which both $\overline{U}$ and $\beta \overline{U}$ are self-similar profiles for some nontrivial $\beta$. Homothetic solutions are, in addition, the only solutions for which a singular limit argument can be used to prove non-uniqueness of Leray-Hopf solutions along the lines of the Jia-\v{S}ver\'{a}k program. In three dimensions, and for sufficiently regular initial data, we prove a Liouville theorem that rules out the existence of non-trivial homothetic solutions. In two dimensions, our Liouville theorem reproves a result of Luo and Shvydkoy that the only decaying homothetic solution with continuous angular data is the Oseen vortex. In addition, we prove that the Euler equations linearized around the Oseen vortex are stable in some subspaces of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$, for example in the space of $2$-fold rotationally symmetric functions. On the other hand, we also discover a homothetic solution for which an unstable approximate eigenvalue of the linearized Euler equations exists.
item.dc:creator: Tim Binz, Matei P. Coiculescu

item.title: Large Solutions for Fractional Laplacian on Infinite Cylindrical Domains
item.description: arXiv:2607.25906v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate large solutions of linear and semi-linear equations involving the fractional Laplacian on domains that are becoming unbounded in some, but not all, directions. Solutions that blow up on the boundary of a domain are commonly called large solutions. For local operators, such behaviour arises only in the presence of lower-order nonlinear terms. However, for nonlocal operators, the existence of such solutions is more subtle. In contrast to the local case, the nonlocal nature of the operator gives rise to different boundary blow-up phenomena even in the case of linear equations. In this article, we study the existence and qualitative behaviour of boundary blow-up solutions to fractional linear and semi-linear equations on finite cylindrical domains and employ these properties to construct large solutions on infinite cylinders.
item.dc:creator: Indranil Chowdhury, N N Dattatreya

item.title: Failure of fixed-profile modified scattering and generalized modified scattering for the 1D defocusing cubic NLS
item.description: arXiv:2608.02534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the one-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with initial data in $L^2(\mathbb R)$. We first prove that the standard fixed-profile modified-scattering ansatz fails at the unweighted $L^2$ endpoint for the one-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation. More precisely, there exists a real-valued datum $$u_*\in L^1(\mathbb R)\cap\bigcap_{m\in\mathbb N}H^m(\mathbb R), \qquad xu_*\notin L^2(\mathbb R).,$$ for which the corrected Fourier profile has no strong $L^2$ limit. Secondly, for every $L^2$ datum, we prove generalized modified scattering: in the physical ray coordinates $x=2tz$, the rescaled solution admits a strong $L^2$ asymptotic representation whose amplitude is the square root of the conserved transmission density and whose unit complex phase is determined by the initial datum.
item.dc:creator: Xi Chen

item.title: Regularization and H\"older continuity for complex Hessian equations on Hermitian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2608.15552v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a compact Hermitian manifold, and let $\Gamma$ be a symmetric convex cone. We develop a quantitative regularization method for $\Gamma$-admissible functions. As an application, we prove H\"older continuity for every pluripotential solution of complex $m$-Hessian equations whose right-hand sides belong to $L^p$, for $p>\frac{n}{m}$. These results extend to a more general class of complex Hessian equations satisfying the structural condition used by Guo--Phong--Tong.
item.dc:creator: Yulun Xu

item.title: Polynomial mixing for stochastic viscous conservation law equation on the whole line
item.description: arXiv:2608.29824v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of the viscous conservation law equation on the whole real line, subject to a white-in-time force and arbitrarily small damping and viscosity constants. We establish polynomial mixing rates in two settings: (a) a general super-quadratic flux with hyperviscous dissipation, where the growth of the nonlinearity is controlled by the order of hyperviscosity, and the force is sufficiently non-degenerate on a generic L2-basis; and (b) a general quadratic flux with standard second-order dissipation, and the force is non-degenerate on some unconditional basis. Both settings include the classical Burgers-type nonlinearity. The proof is based on an abstract polynomial coupling criterion developed in arXiv:2408.00592 and a Foia\c{s}--Prodi estimate.
item.dc:creator: Peng Gao, Liying Li

item.title: A globally defined compressible polyconvex isotropic energy satisfying the true-stress-true-strain monotonicity condition (TSTS-M++)
item.description: arXiv:2609.06026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a compressible isotropic energy on $\mathrm{GL}^+(3)$ combining polyconvexity and global true-stress-true-strain monotonicity (TSTS-M++), answering a question of Wollner, Holzapfel and Neff. For every $\mu>0$ and $k>0$, the energy $W_k(F)=\frac{\mu}{2k}[\exp(k(\lVert F\rVert^2+3J^{-1}+J-7))-1]$, $J=\det F$, is polyconvex and strictly rank-one convex. Its Cauchy-stress response satisfies TSTS-M++ globally if and only if $k\ge1/(8\sqrt3)$. The reference state is stress free with positive infinitesimal shear and bulk moduli. Stress bijectivity has the smaller sharp threshold $k_{\rm B}\approx0.0083$: at equality the stress map is a global homeomorphism with a nondifferentiable inverse, and above it a global smooth diffeomorphism. Thus, for $k_{\rm B}\le k<1/(8\sqrt3)$, the Cauchy-stress map remains globally bijective while TSTS-M++ fails at finite strain. In the TSTS-M++ regime, each prescribed inner radius of a finite plane-strain annulus with a traction-free outer wall has a unique radial equilibrium, and the inner pressure increases smoothly and strictly from zero to infinity. Comparisons with other energies distinguish the roles of polyconvexity, TSTS-M++, reduced convexity and endpoint growth. Under incompressible spherical inflation, global pressure inversion holds for the Demiray family with $b\ge b_*$, including $W_k|_{J=1}$ for $k\ge k_*$ and the stress-free $I_1$-exponential energy, and for the exponentiated Hencky energy when $k_{\mathrm{eH}}>3/8$. Incompressible neo-Hooke instead has a limit point. A further compressible $I_1$ energy retains the global constitutive properties and reference moduli of $W_k$ but exhibits two pressure turning points under incompressible spherical inflation, showing that these properties allow a descending pressure branch.
item.dc:creator: Dongxin Bai, Yunhao Wu, Yong Li, Kai Zhang, Patrizio Neff

item.title: Modified scattering for semiclassical Bose-Fermi mixtures
item.description: arXiv:2609.06143v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Vlasov-Hartree system models a mixture of bosons and fermions interacting via Coulomb forces in which the bosons are described quantum-mechanically, while the fermions are described classically. For small initial data, we prove that the system exhibits modified scattering, i.e. the bosonic and fermionic subsystems each converge to solutions of the free Schr\"odinger and Vlasov equations respectively, but with coupled logarithmic corrections owing to the long-range nature of Coulomb interactions. We use a mixed Lagrangian and Fourier-based approach to derive explicit descriptions of the asymptotic dynamics of the solution and associated fields and Lagrangian trajectories. Notably, due to our purely Lagrangian analysis on the Vlasov side, we require no derivatives on the initial fermion density, the asymptotic fermionic profile is as regular as the initial data, and convergence occurs in almost the same space as the initial data.
item.dc:creator: Kieran Cavanagh

item.title: Critical Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities via nonlinear scaling argument
item.description: arXiv:2609.28038v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show functional inequalities with logarithmic weights as a critical case of Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities. Original CKN inequalities have polynomial weights and are shown via scaling argument. In this paper, we develop this argument into it for nonlinear scaling. Our inequalities are generalizations of critical Hardy type inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Megumi Sano, Yerkin Shaimerdenov, Hinako Sugimura

item.title: Scattering below the ground state for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical NLS
item.description: arXiv:2609.30228v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with initial data below the ground-state energy and gradient thresholds. This extends the seminal result of Kenig and Merle (Invent. Math., 2006) to general data in $\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)$. Classical concentration compactness and the exclusion of rapid frequency cascades reduce the problem to the quasi-soliton scenario. The main ingredient is a frequency-localized interaction Morawetz estimate based on an explicit convex weight whose time-dependent radius is determined implicitly by the mass density of the high-frequency component. The ground-state gap controls the focusing contribution with constants independent of the mass of this component. The radius is chosen to retain quartic spacetime control, while the continuity equation expresses the moving-radius contribution as a nonnegative square, up to frequency-truncation errors. We absorb these errors by closing the Morawetz estimate together with an auxiliary spacetime bound for the nonlinearity. The resulting quartic bound excludes the quasi-soliton scenario and completes the proof.
item.dc:creator: Qingtang Su, Zehua Zhao

item.title: Regularity for $H$-systems of bounded distortion
item.description: arXiv:2610.06441v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider weak solutions $u \in W^{1,n}(U,\mathbf{R}^{n+1})$ of the $H$-system $- \operatorname{div} ( |\mathrm{D} u|^{n-2} \mathrm{D} u ) = (H \circ u) \, \mathbf{J} u$, where $n \ge 2$, $U$ is the open unit ball in $\mathbf{R}^n$, and $H$ is bounded. We show that $u$ is locally bounded if its distortion $|\mathrm{D} u|^n / |\mathbf{J} u|$ is bounded on the set where $|u|$ is large. By a result of Fusco, Kristensen, Leone, and Verde, it follows that $u$ is locally H\"older continuous if $H$ is continuous, and continuously differentiable with locally H\"older continuous derivative if $H$ is locally Lipschitz. The proof pushes forward $|\mathrm{D} u|^{n-2} \mathrm{D} u \circ \mathrm{D} u^*$ by $u$ to a linear functional on continuous compactly supported maps of $\mathbf{R}^{n+1}$ into $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{R}^{n+1},\mathbf{R}^{n+1})$, whose values on derivatives are controlled by the equation. When the distortion is bounded, this functional satisfies the hypotheses of an inequality of Michael-Simon type for measures satisfying a first-order partial differential equation, due to De Philippis, Gennaioli, Pigati,and Rindler. The inequality yields lower bounds for the mass ratios of the push-forward of $|\mathrm{D} u|^n \mathscr{L}^n$ by $u$, and these imply boundedness.
item.dc:creator: S{\l}awomir Kolasi\'nski

item.title: Interior regularity of mixed local-nonlocal parabolic semilinear equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.06537v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we prove the existence, uniqueness and regularity of classical solutions \break of a semilinear parabolic equation with a mixed local and nonlocal diffusion operator \break $\mathcal{L} = -(-\Delta)^s + \Delta$ and Dirichlet boundary conditions. Here, $(-\Delta)^s$ is the integral fractional laplacian and $\Delta$ is the classic local laplacian. We then study the interior regularity of said solutions and conclude that they are H\"older continuous in both space and time, and they are $C^{2,\alpha}_{loc}$ in space for all positive times.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Junquera, Leandro M. Del Pezzo

item.title: The $L^1$-realization of an elliptic operator with unbounded coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.06659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an $L^1$-theory for a class of elliptic operators with unbounded coefficients, extending our earlier semigroup generation results and those of Canale--Rhandi--Tacelli to the endpoint $p=1$.
