The $L^1$-realization generates a positive analytic $C_0$-semigroup that is compact for every positive time. We characterize the generator domain through weighted estimates and prove consistency with the corresponding $L^p$-semigroups for $1<p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Sallah Eddine Boutiah

item.title: Global minimality of lamellae for isotropic Ohta--Kawasaki and Yukawa energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.08485v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a sharp comparison principle for the sharp-interface Ohta--Kawasaki energy and its Yukawa-screened counterpart in dimensions $2\le d\le 7$, for $m=0$, and under periodic and zero-flux Neumann boundary conditions. Whenever the finite optimal stripe width is compatible with the domain, we prove global minimality of periodic lamellae and characterize all minimizers. The proof combines radial comparison kernels, a sharp Fourier bound, and rigidity for a directional translation inequality in $BV$. The kernels are positive measures up to dimension five; in dimensions six and seven, distributional lifting and monotonicity of the averaged translation defect yield the same sharp comparison. In the Appendix, we also prove that no finite positive measure with the prescribed Fourier multiplier exists in dimensions $d\ge6$, and explain why the argument does not directly extend to $d \geq 8$.
item.dc:creator: Dario Reggiani

item.title: Blow-down and immediate onset of positivity in the Neumann problem for (super-)fast diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15673v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the degenerate parabolic equation $u_t=\nabla\cdot (u^{m-1}\nabla u)$, the homogeneous Neumann problem in smoothly bounded domains $\Omega\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ is considered in the (super-fast) diffusion range when $m\in (-\infty,1)$. Upper and lower estimates for solutions are inferred by means of two Moser-type iterations, and optimality properties of these bounds are derived using comparison arguments. On the basis of the accordingly obtained information on regularization into spaces of bounded and uniformly positive functions, a result on global solvability in an associated initial-boundary value problem is achieved for all nonnegative and nontrivial initial data belonging to $L^1(\Omega) \cap \bigcup_{s>n(1-m)/2} L^s(\Omega)$.
item.dc:creator: Youshan Tao, Michael Winkler

item.title: Global well-posedness for a damped two dimensional fluid--beam system
item.description: arXiv:2610.18310v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the normalized surface system of an irrotational incompressible fluid of infinite depth beneath an elastic Euler--Bernoulli beam with structural damping. For every fixed damping coefficient $\gamma>0$, we establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial data in $H^2(\R)\times\bigl(\dot H^{1/2}(\R)\cap\dot H^1(\R)\bigr)$. The main novelty is that the admissible data include finite energy initial potentials for which neither $\psi_0$ nor $u_0=\psi_0+G(\eta_0)\psi_0$ has an $L^2$ representative. We also prove the exact energy dissipation identity at the regularity of the constructed solutions. The main analytical difficulties are the possible failure of $L^2$ integrability at low frequencies and the justification of energy differentiation at the solution regularity. To handle the low-frequency difficulty, we fix the low-frequency part of the initial potential and evolving an $L^2$ remainder. Homogeneous Dirichlet--Neumann estimates and a high-frequency Fourier symmetrizer yield local well-posedness with $H^{-1}$ forcing. Continuous Fr\'echet differentiability of the energy in these affine coordinates, together with a chain rule on $H^1\subset L^2\subset H^{-1}$, justifies the dissipation identity. The Energy identity and coercivity provide uniform bounds that yields global continuation tharough the local theory. Iterating the local uniqueness and stability estimates gives global uniqueness within the stated affine solution class and Lipschitz dependence on bounded sets over every finite time interval.
item.dc:creator: Weihua Wang, Lu Yang

item.title: Sharp Global Well-Posedness for the Logarithmically Regularized 2D Euler Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18775v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider solutions to the two-dimensional Euler equations with a logarithmically regularized velocity given by $u=\nabla^{\perp}(-\Delta)^{-1}\ln^{-\gamma}(|\nabla|+e)\omega$ and initial vorticity in $\dot{H}^1 \cap \dot{H}^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We show that if $\gamma>1/2$, then global well-posedness holds.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Radke

item.title: On the Spectrum of Schr\"{o}dinger Operators Interacting at Two Distinct Scales
item.description: arXiv:2509.02587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Schr\"{o}dinger operators of the form $\Delta - W$ on $L^2_{\text{rad}}(\mathbb{R}^3)$, the space of radially symmetric square integrable functions, are relevant in a variety of physical contexts. The potential $W$ is taken to be radially symmetric (i.e. $W(x) = W(|x|)$) and to decompose into two components with distinct spatial scales: $W=W_\varepsilon:= V_0+V_{1,\varepsilon}$. The second component $V_{1,\varepsilon}(|x|) = \varepsilon^2V_1(\varepsilon |x|)$ represents a scaled potential that becomes increasingly delocalized as $\varepsilon \to 0$. We will assume that both potentials $V_0(r), V_1(r)$ exhibit certain decay properties as $r \to \infty$. We show how the eigenvalue count on the positive real axis is built out of the spectra associated with the two reduced eigenvalue problems on their separate scales. The result is that the total number of eigenvalues of $\Delta - W$ is the sum of the number of positive eigenvalues of $\Delta - V_0$ and $\Delta - V_1$. Our analysis combines dynamical systems techniques with a separation of scales argument, providing a novel framework for studying spectral properties of differential operators where multiple spatial scales interact.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Fleurantin, Jeremy L. Marzuola, Christopher K. R. T. Jones

item.title: Continuum Limit of Nonlocal Electrostatics in Random Media
item.description: arXiv:2609.06354v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive a two-scale continuum limit for the electrostatic energy of random charge density fields that are stationary and ergodic under lattice translations. Each microscopic cell is charge neutral in every realization, while its dipole moment may fluctuate and have a nonzero mean. Under assumptions on the stationary microscopic potential and the finite-volume fields, the local and nonlocal energies converge almost surely to deterministic limits. The local limit consists of the ensemble-averaged microscopic Coulomb energy and a cell-depolarization term, whereas the effective polarization determines the nonlocal limit. The cell-depolarization terms cancel in the total energy, which consists of the ensemble-averaged microscopic cell energy and the macroscopic electrostatic field energy. The deterministic specialization recovers the periodic two-scale limit. For an independent-cell random-displacement model, we verify the assumptions of the continuum-limit theorem and show that centered microscopic fluctuations can change the local energy without changing the effective polarization or the nonlocal energy.
item.dc:creator: Prashant K. Jha, Kaushik Dayal
